chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who vomits in his clothes. Is it permissible for him to pray in it without washing it? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is vomit considered impure (najis) in Shia jurisprudence, and does one need to wash clothes to pray if they vomit on them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that vomit does not constitute *najis* (impurity) requiring washing for the validity of prayer, reflecting the Shia juristic view that only specific substances render clothing impure. This ruling highlights the principle of *istishab al-taharah* (presumption of purity), allowing believers to pray in their current garments unless there is definitive knowledge of a specific impurity, thereby easing the burden of ritual cleanliness in daily worship.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddiq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who vomits in his clothes. Is it allowed for him that he prays Salāt in it and he has not washed it?’ Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who vomits in his clothes, if he can perform Salah (prayer) in them without washing. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not an offense to do so.’”
